newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber marked by light buying, ends weak.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber marked by light buying, ends weak.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market closed weakly on Friday with some buyers engaged in light buying to cover positions on forward months, dealers said.
"There's some buying going on, but I don't think the volumes were that heavy. I did not see the major consumers in the market so action remained a bit slack," one dealer said.
Traders said many consumers who had bought a lot of material for forward delivery were not in a hurry to buy and were holding off to see how much lower prices would go.
The bulk of the buying was in RSS3 grade rubber, especially for prompt June delivery.
"I did not see much action in rubber today. Interest is really thin," a trader said.
"The big boys are not really around. It's difficult to generate any excitement in this kind of a market," another dealer said.
Lower prices in the Tokyo rubber market provided a bearish backdrop to the market and kept most people sidelined.
At 0945 GMT, June RSS3 was seen unchanged at 108.00 U.S. cents a kg. June RSS1 was seen at 156.00 Singapore cents (US$1.08) a kg from 156.25 cents.
